questions.q: According to this lesson, when should design decisions for a dashboard begin?
options: Only after every visual has already been built
Only after the dashboard has been shared with its audience
Design decisions don't matter as long as the data is correct
Before opening Power BI and dragging any visual onto the canvas
questions.explain: Understanding the audience and their needs comes first — skipping this step is how a dashboard ends up technically correct but practically useless.

questions.q: What is one of the four audience questions this lesson highlights?
options: What key metrics help your audience make decisions?
Which color theme looks best on a phone screen?
What is the maximum row count Power BI supports?
How many visuals can fit on one page?
questions.explain: This question forces you to filter down to the numbers that actually change what the audience does next, rather than everything the data could show.

questions.q: Why is a dashboard described as an 'overview, not a detail dump'?
options: Detail data can never be connected to a dashboard
Dashboards technically cannot contain more than five visuals
Dashboards are only for executives, never for detailed analysis
It sits on top of underlying reports and semantic models that already hold the detail, which viewers can drill into
questions.explain: Since readers can always drill into a full report from a dashboard tile, the dashboard itself should show only what someone needs to monitor at a glance.

questions.q: Why does it matter where and how a dashboard will be viewed?
options: It only matters for the color scheme, not the amount of content
A dashboard on a large monitor can hold more content than one viewed on a phone, which affects layout decisions made later
It has no effect on design — dashboards look identical on every device
Viewing location only matters after the dashboard is finished
questions.explain: Deciding this upfront is cheaper than redesigning a finished dashboard around it later — it directly affects layout and content density decisions in later lessons.

questions.q: What's the recommended way to turn the four audience questions into something actionable?
options: Memorize them mentally without writing anything down
Write the answers down as a short brief before building anything, to serve as a reference point for design decisions
Skip them entirely if the deadline is tight
Only apply them after the dashboard is already built, as a final check
questions.explain: A short written brief becomes the reference point for which KPIs make the cut, what goes in the most prominent position, and what story the dashboard needs to tell.
